content.thinking:
I'm planning the bookshelf design carefully—roughly 1.6m wide, 0.4m deep, 2.1m tall—thinking through how to structure it as plain objects with a single root joint as required by the builder API.

I'll add a hinge joint for a hanging sign to keep things simple, and write a small helper function that places parts with a default bone of "root" so attachment stays predictable across all the pieces: base plinth, crown arch with gold trim, twisted side pillars, four shelf levels, a starry-textured back panel, and varied book items.

To stay under the part limit, I'm grouping books by color and merging their geometries into single parts, with separate thin gold boxes merged as spine bands. I'm setting up a merge collector that accumulates geometries per color, applies transforms, and flushes each group into one combined part at the end -- keeping flat-colored geometry mergeable while reserving painted cel-shaded textures for the few larger pieces like the frame, shelves, and back panel.

I'm weighing whether merged book clusters can still get cel-shaded paint colors rather than flat materials, since paint baking should work fine on merged geometry positioned at origin. The tradeoff is that spreading paint across many merged parts lowers texel density, though for flat color regions with hard edges that's probably acceptable.

Now I'm sketching out the overall structure: a plinth with gilded feet, side panels, cornice, shelving, and a back panel that could carry a starry indigo paint pattern, while glow elements need to stay flat-colored rather than painted.

Writing crown arch outline...

Still generating outline points...

Adding a moon emblem decal on the crown face with glow emissive, then planning twisted pillar columns with gold bands and lathe-based capitals/bases at the front corners.

I'm using LatheGeometry for pillar bases, orb stands, candlesticks, and potions throughout the merge bag, then laying out the shelf interior with side panels, front pillars at x=±0.90, and shelf boards spaced vertically from y=0.25 up to the top board near 2.0.

I'm working out the vertical spacing so each of the four compartments has enough clear height once I account for the 0.04 board thickness, adjusting shelf top positions (0.25, 0.75/0.80, 1.25/1.35, 1.75/1.90) so the top row doesn't end up too cramped against the ceiling underside at 2.04.

Adding the top board above the shelves and stacking the crown on top gets me to roughly 2.7m total, which feels quite tall for a fantasy wizard bookshelf — I could shrink the crown height to bring it down to about 2.55m. Now I'm sketching the plinth base dimensions underneath.

Above the plinth I'm planning a cabinet base skirt with a frieze panel that could carry gold inlay decoration, then defining the side panels' dimensions and positioning the back panel as a thin board set further inward.

Still defining dimensions...

Still defining pillar geometry...

Now adding candles: brass lathed candlesticks with cream cylinder bodies, wax drips as small spheres, and glowing orange flame shapes, all merged by color and grouped into solid vs. glowing bags keyed by color and glow strength.

I'm narrowing the crown's base width to leave shoulder space on the top board, so I can place a candelabra and other small items on either side without overlapping the crown's outline.

On the shoulders I'll add a candelabra with three dripping candles on the left and an owl figurine on the right—ellipsoid body, ear tufts, glowing eyes, wings, and feet—for a wizardy touch. I'm also considering adding a small hanging pendulum as the one moving element.

I need a root joint since all meshes likely need a bone reference, so I'll set up a "root" joint at the origin for everything to attach to, and keep just one hinge for simplicity—maybe an open book with a hinged cover rather than a hanging sign or lantern.

Actually, let me add floor clutter to dress the scene: a stack of books with a dripping candle and a scroll on the left, and on the right a small chest with a hinged lid joint plus a crystal orb on a tripod stand, widening the scene to about 2.9 meters.

Working out the hinge rotation math, I determine opening the lid requires a negative rotation angle about the X-axis, so I'll build the lid in its closed position and then pose the joint at -50 degrees to swing it open, with the hinge joint defined at the back edge aimed along +Z.

Now I'm placing the floor decorations: a glowing gold coin pile inside the chest, a crystal orb on a tripod stand to the right glowing cyan/violet, and I'm figuring out positions for a candle cluster and book stack so nothing overlaps the chest on the left side.

Overall bounds come out to about 3 meters wide. Now I'm working out the shelf contents: generating rows of books with randomized thickness, height, and depth, varying some leaning and some stacked, each with a colored cover and a cream page block visible at the spine-facing side.

I'm adding spine details like gold bands and a title plate, then reconsidering the geometry: with the spine facing the viewer, the top view should show the thin spine strip at front and the covers running front-to-back as side walls, with pages visible between them.

So I'm building each book from merged boxes - a spine box, two cover plates, and a pages block - and grouping them by material color (cover, pages, gold bands) to keep triangle counts low across the roughly 70 books.

For placement, I'm using a transform helper that builds a matrix combining translation and z-rotation so each book can tilt at an angle on the shelf. I'm also planning decoration variants per book - plain gold bands, gems, labels, or straps - plus a few standout pieces like an open spellbook on an easel.

Now I'm mapping out shelf rows by x-position: one row for a dense stack of books, potion bottles, and a jar cluster in the middle, another for lying tomes with candles, and a top row for crystal orbs on stands alongside more books and scrolls.

For R3 I'm adding an armillary sphere centerpiece made of gold torus rings with a small orb inside, plus candles with melted wax and lit flame glow on the top shelf. I'm also planning hanging crystal pendants with gold chains under the top board, and cheap cobweb decal textures tucked into the top corners for atmosphere.

I'm placing two small translucent cobweb planes in back corners using alpha-cut textures, facing forward. For the crown I'm adding a glowing moon emblem decal, a row of gold stars, gold rim trim, and an octahedron crystal finial at the peak with small pointed spires as acroteria at the crown's base ends.

Now I'm detailing the side panels with thin gold frame boxes forming inset rectangles plus rune decals, and adding a cornice moulding strip along the top board where the crown sits, before moving on to settling the overall color palette of deep indigo and wine tones.

I'm picking specific hex values: warm reddish-brown wood with darker grain lines, navy backing, gold accents in bright and darkened tones, cream highlights, and a varied set of jewel-tone colors for the book spines like ruby, teal, indigo, violet, forest green, orange, sky blue, rose, and plum.

I'm staying mindful of the 64 flat colour limit, planning to reuse a cached cel paint per hex value so repeated colours don't multiply unnecessarily, while glow effects use separate flat colour strings. I'm also considering how curved lathe geometry will interpolate normals smoothly at paint boundaries, and thinking through how paint baking requirements might affect the small merged box shapes.

I'll skip per-book rune textures as overkill and go with gold bands and labels instead, maybe cream cel tones for parchment/scroll elements. Now I'm starting to write the actual code, importing three.js and the geometry merge utility to begin assembling the builder.

Setting up imports and the build function...

I'm settling on a cleaner object-based API for adding shapes, taking color, glow, geometry, position, rotation, and optional non-uniform scale, and noting I'll need to fix normals after applying the transform matrix.

For merging, I need every geometry to share the same attribute set and be indexed, so I'm avoiding Octahedron/Icosahedron (non-indexed Polyhedron) and instead using a low-segment Sphere for crystal shapes, plus Lathe, Cone, Cylinder, Torus, and Plane since those are all indexed with consistent uv/normal attributes. Now I'm writing the flush function that iterates through grouped geometry lists to merge them.

Writing merge logic...

I also need to key the bag by bone (root vs lid) since lid parts attach differently, and I'm setting up a paint cache keyed by string with a Paint type import.

Adding box helper functions...

Still defining geometry...

Still writing book placement logic...

Still tuning depth values...

Finishing the fill function and adding a leaning end book for visual variety, tilting it slightly against the shelf to break up the straight row.

I also need a helper for books lying horizontally rather than standing upright, rotating the geometry so the spine faces outward correctly while keeping the deterministic RNG stream consistent.

Working through the orientation logic: with spine facing front, the fore-edge opens toward the back, so the cream page block should recess at the head/tail ends (top/bottom), visible as a thin line when the pages box is sized slightly smaller than the covers. I'll apply the same recessed-pages trick for the standing orientation, viewed from the top.

Now I'm defining helper functions for scene composition: a stacking function for lying books that layers them by thickness increments with optional yaw rotation and offsets, decorative bands as thin boxes positioned along the spine, and a scroll function that builds a parchment-colored cylinder rotated to lie along the z-axis with darker rolled end caps for a realistic look.

Still writing scroll details...

For the pyramid arrangement of scrolls in the left section, I'm laying out rows of smaller cylinders in a triangular stacking pattern, with each row offset in x and y and varying ribbon colors for visual distinction.

Now I'm designing a mystical orb with a lathed golden stand (base disc, stem, cup) holding a glowing sphere, and considering how to texture its surface with a galaxy swirl effect using a radial gradient and sparkle pattern.

Still defining stand profile...

Still writing lathe profile points...

Now I'm designing a tall candelabra for the left shoulder, using a lathed stem with torus-arc arms curving outward from the stem to form U-shaped side branches holding candles.

Now I'm designing an owl perched on the right shoulder: a feathered body with a lighter belly patch, a round head with ear tufts, glowing yellow eyes with black pupils, an orange beak, squashed side wings, small feet, and a tiny stone plinth base, oriented slightly toward center.

I'm adding a cute tiny purple wizard hat with stars on the owl's head, then designing a treasure chest with a wooden body banded in gold, corner studs, a lock plate, glowing coins inside, and a half-cylinder lid shape for the curved top.

Working out the half-cylinder rotation math...

Combining this with the rotZ(90) step, the Euler order 'XYZ' in three.js applies Rz first then Ry then Rx, which matches what I need for the arch orientation. I'm also setting the geometry's theta start to -π/2 so the half-cylinder cross-section aligns correctly along x and z.

For the lid, I'm placing it in model coordinates as if closed, with its hinge at the back top edge of the body and its arch half-cylinder running along the x-axis -- no non-uniform squashing needed since I'm just adjusting the radius to make the arch shallower than it is wide. Inside the chest I'm planning a small pile of flattened gold spheres near the top to suggest coins sitting just below the rim.

Now I'm positioning the coin mound to poke slightly above the body's top surface so it reads clearly, and setting up the lid's hinge joint with a rotation axis so opening the lid reveals the glowing coins beneath the arch. I'm also adding thin decorative bands across the lid using narrow half-cylinders to simulate gold trim.

For the scroll basket, I'm designing a woven-look cylinder with a dark top cap suggesting depth inside, with scroll rods poking out the top, and considering painted stripe details to fake a woven texture.

Woven checker pattern using UV coordinates, applied to the basket geometry, plus a gold rim torus and handle, with vertical scroll cylinders of varying heights sticking up inside. Now sketching out a large orb stand for the right side.

For the orb I'm building a tripod of three gold rods supporting a sphere around y=0.78 with r=0.16, plus a tilted gold ring around it and six tiny glowing cyan octahedra floating nearby as sparkles. Then I'm shifting to plan a tall stack of tomes on a plinth for the left side.

I'm positioning the book stack and chest to avoid overlap, piling five lying tomes with varied yaw and accumulating heights, then topping them with a melted candle with wax puddle and flame plus a small potion bottle. I'm also considering adding a round rug under the whole group, painted with concentric wine-colored rings using a radial distance function from a shifted center.

Writing rug pattern code...

I'm tapering the petal widths so they shrink outward, and checking that the rug thickness lets items sink slightly without exceeding the allowed tolerance against the floor. I'm also verifying the rug's painted surface area and texel density look reasonable for both top and bottom faces.

Given total painted area across shelves and other surfaces is around 50 m², I'm settling on a 2048 paint size with a 4096 atlas for adequate detail, accepting the rug pattern will be a bit coarse but acceptable. For the back panel, I'm writing a star-field pattern using layered cell noise to scatter small gold and cream star dots across the surface.

For the rest, I'm defining gradient backgrounds mixing navy and purple tones for depth, and setting up grain-based wood paints with different axis orientations for vertical versus horizontal boards, using a cel-shaded lighting wrapper so each wood paint responds to shadow correctly, then starting a darker wood variant for the plinth.

Now I'm sketching the stone plinth texture and planning rod-based pillars with circular cross-sections, where the paint function uses angle calculations to create alternating gold and purple striped patterns around each pillar.

Working out the pillar caps and capitals using lathe profiles for base and top shapes, plus adding a glowing cyan gem sphere at the pillar top so the pillars extend above the top board within its footprint.

Checking whether the pillar protrudes outside the carcass edges, comparing the pillar's radius and position against the carcass front face to confirm it stays flush rather than sticking out.

Good merging there. I'm placing decorative rune texture decals on the side panels with gold frame trim, sized and positioned to sit flush against the carcass sides with proper orientation, and I'm starting to think about adding carved shelves next.

Skipping the carved star cutouts for simplicity, I'm adding a gold diamond inlay plus small glowing rune accents to the front bottom panel, and considering small gold knob spheres under the shelf ends instead of brackets, along with a thin gold lip strip along each shelf's front edge.

Now I'm adding small gold stud spheres spaced along that lip, then planning hanging pendants beneath the top board -- thin gold chain cylinders with glowing gem spheres (violet and cyan) dropping into the third row, while sketching out how books and the armillary sphere will be positioned across that row.

Working through the right side, I'm placing orbs on stands flanking the central armillary sphere, then a candle trio of varying heights plus a scroll jar further right, checking that pendant chains hanging at ±0.18-0.2 clear the armillary's ring radius and don't collide with the orbs.

For the second shelf, I'm laying out leaning books on the left, an hourglass and potion bottles in the middle, and a stack of lying books on the right. For the bottles I'm thinking through how to render them with painted liquid colors and a small white highlight box to suggest glass, since true transparency isn't straightforward here, and considering adding a cauldron for more magical atmosphere.

Moving to the first shelf, I'm mapping out a scroll pyramid on the left, books with a bookend, and a glowing spellbook on a lectern in the center—built from a gold lathe stand plus two tilted page boxes rotated slightly apart to form an open book look, sitting atop its covers.

I'm working out the rotation math so the open book tilts back correctly to face the viewer, using a rotation around the X axis by 55 degrees so its normal points up and outward, then placing the individual pages within that tilted parent frame.

For the rune text, I need the plane facing up rather than forward, so I rotate it -90° around X, and I'm planning two textured planes for the rune glow on each page. On the right side I'm adding a small glowing orb on a stand, plus a candle near the lectern.

On the left shelf I'm stacking tall books and placing a glowing jar cluster in the center—maybe a wide purple potion jar with a cork lid, or a cute little iron cauldron with glowing green liquid, tiny feet, and a handle. On the right I'm laying out a stack of four large books with a candle on top, plus a bookend.

Beyond that, I'm considering optional floating elements, but I'm keeping the budget tight. For atmosphere, I'm adding cobweb textures as simple SVG planes tucked into the corners, radiating lines from the top-left apex, positioned at the back near the short books so they read naturally without conflicting with the main objects.

I'll also plan sparkly diamond-shaped glow accents scattered around the shelf crown—maybe ten of them in cyan and gold tones—and give the crown panel a deep indigo mottled finish for richness.

For the crown emblem, I'm designing a crescent moon with gold and cyan stars, sizing it to fit the crown's arched outline, and working out its exact position and dimensions so it's centered nicely within the peak.

Writing crown outline code...

Writing outline generation function...

Placing the crown-base corner cones and candle flames with glow, then working out chest and stack positioning near the rug—keeping axes aligned and spacing the chest and stack coordinates so they fit within the rug radius without overlapping.

Setting up the orb, basket, and verifying the rug covers the full layout. Now I'm starting to write the actual TypeScript code, defining helper types and an `add` function to manage geometry grouping by color and bone...

Writing helper function...

Adding more geometry helpers...

Working out the normal direction formula: for a profile segment with direction (dx,dy) in the (radius,height) plane, the outward normal is (dy,-dx). Moving upward gives an outward-facing normal, moving outward at the bottom gives a downward-facing normal, and moving inward at the top gives an upward-facing normal — confirming my closed profile ordering (axis-bottom → out → up → in) produces correct outward orientation.

Setting up a color palette of hex constants for gold, cream, parchment, wax, cyan, violet, flame, and other material tones to use across the model.

Now I'm writing a book-building function that positions a tilted box using a transform matrix, then adds a spine box and side boxes to construct a book shape...

Adding pages and gold bands...

Now I'm designing variations: style 0 gets a glowing cyan gem, style 1 doubles the bands, style 2 adds a label with ink lines, and style 3 gets a rotated gold diamond emblem.

I also need a scroll function that builds a parchment cylinder core with a darker inner layer and a ribbon wrap, oriented along its length.

Now I'm designing a potion bottle function with a glowing round base and a tapered neck, using a lighter glassy color for the neck and planning a cork on top.

I'm also adding a small white specular highlight on the sphere's surface to simulate glass shine, and figuring out how to wrap a cream-colored label band around the bottle's equator without it poking through the sphere.

Now I'm starting to define a flame helper function...

Now I'm sketching out the candle function, starting with an optional holder shape using a lathe profile for the base.

Planning out the color variants and drip placement with deterministic angles, then working out the shelf layout constants—row heights, board positions, and center coordinates for the bottom block, shelves, and top board.

Still writing shelf geometry...

Still placing trim and plinth details...

Now I'm planning the remaining decorative pieces to build: owl, candelabra, chest, orb stands, basket, floating stars, armillary sphere, hourglass, lectern book, cauldron, cobweb, and crown emblem. For the armillary, I'm constructing a gold lathe base with a stem and three intersecting torus rings at different rotations to form the classic sphere shape.

Still designing hourglass geometry...

Now I'm shaping the cauldron with a lathe profile for the iron body.

Still shaping the cauldron geometry...

Now building the owl figure's body parts layer by layer: torso, belly, and head using scaled spheres positioned relative to its base at the pedestal.

Still placing owl parts...

Still working out arm placement...

Now I'm adding wax drips on the centre candle, then moving to the chest: setting up the body box dimensions and top position, with gold bands and corner studs for decoration.

For the lock plate, I'm adding a small gold box with an inked keyhole, then scattering a mound of coins and gems on top using spheres and small coins with random positions, tilts, and glow colors like ruby red and cyan to make the treasure pile look varied.

For the lid, I'm working out the geometry for a half-cylinder shape rotated into position, carefully tracking how each axis rotation transforms the coordinates so the curved lid sits correctly along the chest's length.

I also need the flat lid plate to avoid intersecting the coin mound beneath it when closed, so I'm planning for the plate to rotate open with the lid at roughly -55 degrees from vertical.

The lid bands are gold half-cylinders slightly larger than the shell radius, and since the cylinder geometry isn't open-ended, the end caps form semicircular discs that close off the shape properly. I'm placing the hinge joint at the back edge of the top, with its rotation axis along x.

I need to call the pose function after everything is built and flushed, applying a -55 degree rotation to set the lid's rest position — since painted parts bake their pattern at build time and retain it through later poses, the ordering matters: build, flush, then pose. I'm also setting up a bone-to-joint mapping type so the bag flush logic can reference joints by bone key.

Now I'm defining the hinge joint for the lid at the top rear edge, confirming that parts with explicit bone assignment and a zero offset tuple avoid weight blending from nearby bones. Then I'm sketching the basket geometry — a tapered cylinder for the weave body with checker-paint UVs, plus a rim torus in gold and dark tones.

Adding scroll parchment cylinders and ribbon details...

Now I'm designing the orb stand with three gold-colored strut legs angled outward from a center point, computed using a helper function connecting two points with a given radius.

Still writing orb texture SVG...

I'm defining a star-field paint function that blends a deep blue-violet base with cell-based bright stars, tuning star size against texel resolution, and considering layering in nebula noise on top.

Writing rug paint function...

Still defining color zones...

Now I'm checking chest placement bounds against the cylinder radius, then moving on to writing the main file with glow effects applied to merged parts, and sketching a cobweb SVG with radiating stroke paths.

Writing cobweb lines and arcs... Then I work out plane placement by centering on corner offsets, and start on a rune glyph SVG for decorative elements.

Checking the stroke scaling at 512px confirms the raster width works out correctly. Now I'm designing an emblem with a crescent moon shape formed by overlapping arcs and adding small four-pointed star accents in cyan.

Moving to the page runes SVG for the open book, I'm sketching thin cyan stroke marks to suggest tiny glyphs, then verifying the raster scaling again. For the spell sigil I'm adding simple horizontal lines plus a circular mark, and now I'm starting to position and shape the lectern with its open book using a lathe profile for the gold stand base.

Still writing the lectern geometry...

For the plane's orientation, world-up aligns so the drawing's top naturally points upward when projected onto the tilted plane. I need to account for the page's own curvature near the edges where the rune plane sits, since rotating each page about its own center means the plane position shifts slightly relative to the flat approximation I was using.

I'm settling on lifting the plane to 0.021 so it clears the page surface cleanly with no z-fighting, even at the outer edges where the gap would otherwise be razor thin. Now I'm moving to write the actual code, keeping an eye on the total part count across bag groups, painted elements, and textures to stay within budget, and tallying up the distinct color names used across the glow groups.

Writing the import statements...

Still writing lathe geometry and glow orb placement...

Placing sparkle stars near the crown and orb, using a helper that builds small octahedron-like diamonds by crossing two scaled, low-segment spheres to get a faceted sparkle shape.

I'm double-checking total height budget—crown top plus finial crystal lands around 2.6-2.7 units, with floating sparkles allowed to exceed that slightly since they're decorative accents. Now I'm sketching out the shelf rows, placing book clusters and a leaning book at specific x-positions on the lower shelf.

Still placing objects...

For row 3 I'm placing books on the left, a violet orb, the armillary sphere, a cyan orb, and a cluster of candles at different heights on the right, possibly resting on a small lying stack of books.

I'm working out positioning for a corner web above the books, hanging pendants with gems near the armillary sphere, and the lathe geometry for the armillary's base to keep everything aligned without collisions.

Still writing armillary code...

I'm checking the cauldron radius doesn't clip into the book stack, deciding to skip bookend statues, and sketching logic for placing a leaning book at the end of each shelf row.

Adding leaning book positioning...

Now I'm writing a helper function to place lying books, computing a transform matrix that positions and rotates each book around its center with the right offsets for covers and pages.

Adding gold bands and a cream label to finish the book shape, confirming the pages sit recessed within the covers. I'm also setting up owl color variables and planning decorative corbels before writing the full assembly code.

Now I'm positioning the gold frame panels on each side, the rune glow planes, and corner ball accents to flesh out the side ornamentation.

Working on the plinth's front decor: diamond-shaped gold inlays and connecting strip lines positioned across the bottom block's front face, plus the gold overhang lip for the top board.

Now for the crown piece, I'm defining the material setup with a starred panel paint and gold rim, checking the extrude function's parameter options to make sure bone attachment and coloring work correctly. I'm writing a helper function that generates the crown's curved outline shape, computing a falloff curve across its width to create a rounded peak profile.

Checking the geometry alignment -- both the rim and panel outlines start at y=0, and the rim peak sits slightly higher than the panel peak, positioning the gem crystal above both. I'm considering whether to add decorative gold studs or an inlaid arch line along the crown, but deciding to keep it simpler with just an emblem plane and scattered gold sparkle accents instead of a full sweep geometry.

Now I'm working out placement for small gold studs along the rim front, computing their y-position using the crown height curve and offsetting them slightly inward in z to sit just in front of the surface, alongside an emblem plane positioned at a similar depth. I'm also designing a lathe-profile finial cup in gold for the pillar tops, topped with a glowing cyan gem sphere.

I'm figuring out how the pillars, capitals, and board fit together vertically so the cup sits correctly on top, then planning hanging pendant details -- thin chains, scaled glowing gem spheres, and gold cap beads -- plus gold studs along the shelf lips and a reusable book-placement function, before starting to emit the actual code.

Still writing book stack code...

Adding the unrolled parchment with curled ends and ink line details nearby, checking it fits within the rug bounds. I'll skip potions on the floor and think about adding quills next.

Setting up a color cache helper and naming convention for bag parts, then double-checking type compatibility for color fills and vector spreads before finalizing the file write.

Still defining joints and poses...
